items.title: Obtain an Abilene itinerant business permit
items.description: Businesses operating as itinerant businesses in Abilene must obtain the applicable city permit; the current city fee schedule lists an itinerant business permit fee of $150.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Allen
items.description: Review the cited local licensing source before operating; requirements may be activity-specific and can differ by business type or location.

note: No general city business license was found on the city's pages or code; the items cover the hotel occupancy tax, which applies to lodging providers only.

items.title: Register as a lodging provider for Amarillo hotel occupancy tax
items.description: Lodging providers register with the city each year through Localgov, at no fee, by January 1.

items.title: File the Amarillo hotel occupancy tax report
items.description: Lodging providers file a monthly hotel occupancy tax report and payment through Localgov, including a zero return when there was no revenue. The city rate is 7%, plus 2% for the Amarillo-Potter Events Venue District.

items.title: Obtain or renew an Arlington local alcohol permit
items.description: Businesses seeking local alcohol authorization in Arlington apply through the city's permit portal, obtain city approval, and complete the related Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission application.

items.title: Renew an Arlington food-establishment operating permit
items.description: Food establishments in Arlington need the applicable operating permit; the city's current fee schedule lists high-, medium- and low-priority permits as valid for one year from issuance.

items.title: Renew Arlington contractor registration
items.authority: City of Arlington Planning and Development Services
items.description: Contractors performing regulated work in Arlington must meet the city's registration requirements; the city offers one-year and two-year registrations with listed fees.

note: The city's start-a-business page says Texas has no general business license, that most Austin businesses need permits or licenses depending on type, location and activity (issued through Austin Development Services), and lists no general city business license. Business personal property tax is administered by the Travis County Appraisal District, not the city.

items.title: Obtain an Austin certificate of occupancy when required
items.description: Austin issues a certificate of occupancy after successful final inspection for new construction or significant renovations; a change of use may require an updated certificate for a business space.

items.title: Obtain an Austin food enterprise operating permit
items.description: A food business operating in Austin or Travis County must obtain a Food Enterprise Operating Permit; the facility must pass the required pre-opening inspection before the permit is issued and the business operates.

items.title: Obtain a Beaumont certificate of occupancy before opening
items.description: A new building or a change in occupancy in Beaumont cannot be occupied until the city issues a certificate of occupancy; the application requires the business name, address, proposed use and related inspection approvals.

items.title: Obtain a Brownsville certificate of occupancy
items.authority: City of Brownsville Planning and Development Services
items.description: Brownsville requires a certificate of occupancy before a space or building is used or occupied and for changes in use or occupancy, major repairs, alterations or additions; the city lists a $100 CO fee plus a fire-inspection fee.

items.title: Obtain a Brownsville health license for food businesses
items.description: Brownsville states that businesses handling or serving food must contact the health department for a health license before operating.

items.title: Obtain a Carrollton certificate of occupancy
items.description: Carrollton requires a certificate of occupancy for all commercial buildings or suites that are occupied or used; the city lists a $100 certificate fee.

items.title: Obtain a Carrollton fire permit when required
items.description: Carrollton requires a fire permit when a building or business installs, modifies or replaces covered fire alarm, access-control, gate, sprinkler, kitchen-hood, spray-booth or flammable-liquid systems.

items.title: Obtain a College Station certificate of occupancy when required
items.authority: City of College Station Planning & Development Services
items.description: College Station requires a certificate of occupancy for occupancy or use of a newly erected or enlarged building, a change to a different use category, or other cases required by the adopted building code.

note: The current city business and development pages list activity-specific permits, taxes and registrations; no blanket general business license is listed.

items.title: Obtain a Corpus Christi development permit
items.authority: City of Corpus Christi Development Services
items.description: All development in Corpus Christi requires a permit through Development Services.

items.title: Obtain a Corpus Christi certificate of occupancy
items.authority: City of Corpus Christi Development Services
items.description: A building or structure in Corpus Christi may not be used or occupied until the building official issues a certificate of occupancy; commercial construction, remodels, additions and qualifying business-name changes use the applicable certificate process.

note: No official Dallas, Texas page on a general business license was found; a certificate of occupancy applies to premises.

items.title: Renew your Dallas food establishment permit
items.authority: Dallas Code Compliance Services, Consumer Health Division
items.description: Restaurants, bars, grocery stores and other food establishments need an annual Dallas health permit. The city's page lists annual fees of $141 to $513 depending on risk level and size (under or over 2,000 square feet), plus a $121 application fee for a new permit. The annual fee is due December 31. A payment received after December 31 adds a $199 reinstatement fee, and one not paid by January 30 adds a $158 pre-closure fee. A re-inspection costs $191 if the score is below 80%. The page is not dated, so confirm the amounts with the city.

note: The official development code documents a business-registration requirement and activity-specific permits; the complete city obligation set has not yet been entered.

items.title: Obtain a Denton certificate of occupancy
items.description: Denton requires a certificate of occupancy for all new businesses and for changes in use, business name or ownership; the current fee schedule lists a $75 certificate fee.

items.title: Obtain a Denton sign permit
items.description: Denton requires an individual permit for each new sign and requires a certificate of occupancy or building-permit approval before approving a sign permit.

items.title: Obtain a Denton itinerant-merchant permit when applicable
items.description: Solicitors, handbill distributors and itinerant merchants must obtain the applicable Denton permit before conducting that business within the city limits.

items.title: Obtain an Edinburg commercial building permit
items.description: Edinburg's Building Safety Department issues permits and conducts inspections for new construction, alterations, repairs, demolitions and other building operations; commercial applicants use the city's commercial permit process.

note: The Business Licensing Center issues activity-specific licenses (alarm, alcohol and others); a general license was not confirmed.

items.title: Register an El Paso credit access business when applicable
items.authority: City of El Paso Planning and Inspections
items.description: El Paso's credit-access-business application requires a current certificate of occupancy for the business address and a valid state license before the city registration can be processed.

items.title: Obtain a Fort Worth certificate of occupancy
items.authority: City of Fort Worth Development Services
items.description: Every Fort Worth business with a physical location requires a certificate-of-occupancy permit before operating from that location.

items.title: Obtain required Fort Worth commercial building permits
items.authority: City of Fort Worth Development Services
items.description: New commercial construction, additions, remodels, accessory structures and changes of use require the applicable commercial building permits before work proceeds.

items.title: Obtain required Frisco commercial permits
items.description: Frisco requires permits for commercial structures and related work including construction, enlargement, alteration, repair, movement, improvement, removal, conversion or demolition.

items.title: Obtain a Frisco certificate of occupancy
items.description: Frisco provides a certificate-of-occupancy process for new tenants or owners, business-name changes and changes in building use.

note: The city's official business page documents zoning, commercial permits and certificates of occupancy; a complete general-license determination is not yet entered.

items.title: Obtain a Garland certificate of occupancy
items.description: Garland requires a certificate of occupancy for businesses within the city limits; a new certificate is required when ownership, business use or occupied space changes.

items.title: Obtain a Texas sales tax permit when required
items.description: Garland's business occupancy guidance states that businesses must be registered with the State Comptroller and obtain a sales tax permit when applicable.

items.title: Obtain a Grand Prairie certificate of occupancy
items.authority: City of Grand Prairie Building Inspections
items.description: Grand Prairie requires a certificate of occupancy before a commercial building, suite or structure is used or occupied and for changes in use or occupancy; the city states that it does not require a general business license.

items.title: Obtain a Grand Prairie health permit when required
items.authority: City of Grand Prairie Public Health & Environmental Quality
items.description: Grand Prairie requires a health permit when applicable for food service, sales, storage or preparation, day care, chemical storage and similar covered uses.

note: The city issues no general business license; permits are activity-specific (alcohol, coin-operated machines, dealers, game rooms, noise, street vendors). Physical businesses need a certificate of occupancy.

items.title: Renew your Houston food establishment permit
items.description: Any operation that stores, prepares, packages, serves or sells food, such as a restaurant, food warehouse, packaged-food store or commissary, needs a Houston Health Department permit. The permit fee runs from $224.44 to $739.44 depending on risk level, and the permit is valid for one year. Renewal invoices are mailed 30 to 45 days before it expires, and the late fee is $66.21. New construction or a remodel also needs plan review and a preoperational inspection first.

items.title: Renew your Houston mobile food unit medallion
items.description: A food truck, food trailer, ice cream truck or cart needs a mobile food unit medallion from the Houston Health Department. The fee is $258.00 plus a $112.57 inspection fee, and the medallion is valid for one year. A new unit needs plan review and an inspection first. Renewal invoices are mailed 30 to 45 days before it expires.

note: The City of Irving states that it does not issue business permits; businesses may still need activity-specific permits and a certificate of occupancy.

items.title: Obtain a Killeen certificate of occupancy before opening
items.description: Killeen prohibits opening a place of business without a certificate of occupancy; a new CO is required for a change of owner, business name, tenant or use, with a $90 application fee plus a $10 technology fee.

note: Laredo requires new businesses to register and obtain a certificate of occupancy before opening; the complete obligation item has not yet been entered.

items.title: Obtain a Laredo certificate of occupancy before opening
items.authority: City of Laredo Building Development Services
items.description: New Laredo businesses must register with the city and obtain a certificate of occupancy, plus a sign permit when applicable, before opening to the public.

items.title: Obtain a Laredo food truck permit
items.authority: City of Laredo Building Development Services
items.description: Food trucks operating in Laredo apply for the city food truck permit; the city lists a $200 permit fee plus a fire fee determined during review.

items.title: Obtain a Lewisville certificate of occupancy
items.description: Lewisville requires a certificate of occupancy for commercial projects when ownership, tenant, business name or use changes, for new construction, and for enlarged or altered existing buildings; each applicable suite and building requires a separate application.

note: The City of Lubbock states that it does not have a business-licensing process; businesses still need applicable activity, zoning, building, health, and other permits.

items.title: Obtain a McAllen commercial building permit
items.authority: City of McAllen Building Permits & Inspections
items.description: McAllen requires commercial construction work to be submitted through its commercial permit process, and the commercial application states that improvements may not be occupied until a certificate of occupancy is issued.

items.title: Obtain a McAllen sign permit when required
items.description: McAllen requires a sign permit and applicable sign-license registration before erecting, constructing, installing, replacing, renting, leasing or servicing a sign covered by the city code.

items.title: Obtain a McKinney certificate of occupancy
items.description: McKinney provides a commercial certificate-of-occupancy process for new businesses and commercial occupancy, with the certificate allowing the business to operate and be occupied by employees and the public.

items.title: Obtain a McKinney operational fire permit when required
items.authority: City of McKinney Fire Marshal's Office
items.description: McKinney requires operational fire permits for covered businesses or operations such as hazardous materials, high-piled storage, fuel dispensing, propane cylinder exchange and repair garages; permits must be obtained and inspected before the operation begins.

items.title: Obtain a Mesquite certificate of occupancy
items.description: Mesquite requires a certificate of occupancy for commercial properties and before occupancy, use or utility connection; the standard fee is $125 unless the CO is included with a building permit.

items.title: Obtain a Mesquite fire permit when required
items.description: Mesquite Fire Marshal services include permits and inspections for covered systems and activities such as alarms, access control, storage tanks, food trucks, hood suppression, sprinklers and special events.

items.title: Obtain a Midland commercial building permit
items.description: Midland requires a commercial permit for all work performed on commercial structures, and work may begin only after the permit is issued by the city.

items.title: Obtain a Midland certificate of occupancy
items.description: Midland issues a certificate of occupancy after final inspection and completion of required paperwork; the certificate allows the completed space to be used or occupied.

note: Mission states that a business permit must be issued before a business operates; the complete permit requirements and item data have not yet been entered.

items.title: Obtain a Mission business permit before operating
items.description: Mission states that a business permit must be issued before a business officially operates, after all applicable requirements are met.

items.title: Obtain a Mission certificate of occupancy when required
items.description: Mission's commercial building application states that the improvements may not be used until a certificate of occupancy has been issued; the listed issuance fee is $50.

items.title: Obtain an Odessa certificate of occupancy
items.description: Odessa requires a certificate-of-occupancy permit for existing structures and requires the applicable inspections before the space can be occupied or utilities reconnected.

items.title: Register an Odessa contractor when required
items.description: Odessa lists contractor registration for building, remodeling, electrical, plumbing, mechanical and water-well contractors among its municipal permits and licenses.

items.title: Obtain a Pasadena certificate of occupancy
items.description: Pasadena requires a certificate of occupancy before a commercial change in use or occupancy and before utilities are released for the property.

items.title: Obtain a Pearland sign permit
items.description: Pearland requires a sign permit before erecting, installing or modifying a sign; new tenants and business-name changes must have an approved operating certificate or certificate of occupancy before applying.

items.title: Obtain a Pearland certificate of occupancy when required
items.description: Pearland requires a certificate of occupancy before a structure is occupied or used and before a change to a different use occurs.

items.title: Obtain required Plano commercial permits
items.description: Plano provides commercial permitting and certificate-of-occupancy applications through Building Inspections for commercial construction and occupancy work.

items.title: Obtain a Plano food permit for a food facility
items.description: Food facilities in Plano must submit the food permit application and cannot open until the city's certificate of occupancy has been issued.

items.title: Obtain a Richardson certificate of occupancy
items.description: Richardson prohibits use or occupancy, occupancy-classification changes, and tenancy or ownership changes for an existing building or lease space until a certificate of occupancy is issued; the filing fee is $100 unless included with a building permit.

note: The City of Round Rock states that it does not require a general business license; activity-specific permits, contractor registration, alcohol permits, and solicitor permits may still apply.

items.title: Obtain a San Angelo change-of-occupancy permit when required
items.authority: City of San Angelo Permits & Inspections
items.description: San Angelo requires a change-of-occupancy permit when moving into an existing commercial structure if the building use changes; building permits may also be required for alterations or additions.

note: The city has no general business license; the license or permit needed depends on the product or service.

items.title: Obtain a Sugar Land building permit when required
items.authority: City of Sugar Land Permits and Inspections
items.description: Sugar Land requires a permit before a person, firm or corporation erects, constructs, enlarges, alters, repairs, replaces, improves, removes, installs, converts, equips, uses, occupies or maintains a regulated structure or building service equipment.

items.title: Obtain a Sugar Land food permit when applicable
items.authority: City of Sugar Land Food Inspection Program
items.description: Sugar Land's Food Inspection Program permits and inspects temporary, mobile and fixed food establishments operating in the city.

items.title: Obtain a Tyler certificate of occupancy
items.description: Tyler requires a certificate of occupancy for a same-use business space and reviews new business uses through its occupancy process, including floor plans, restroom, exit and parking details.

items.title: Obtain a Waco certificate of occupancy
items.description: Waco requires a certificate of occupancy before initial occupancy and when the occupancy classification, tenancy, ownership, business name or business type changes.

items.title: Obtain a Waco commercial construction permit
items.description: Waco requires approved permits before commercial construction, alteration or renovation work begins; contractors must register before plumbing, electrical or mechanical permits can be issued.

items.title: Obtain a Wichita Falls itinerant-merchant permit when applicable
items.authority: City of Wichita Falls Building and Code Administration
items.description: Wichita Falls requires certain permits and licenses for city operations, including itinerant-merchant permits, solicitor permits, transient-show permits and dealer registration for crafted precious metals.

items.title: Renew Wichita Falls contractor registration
items.authority: City of Wichita Falls Building and Code Administration
items.description: Wichita Falls contractor registration expires one year from issuance; the application warns that work requiring a permit may not begin before permit issuance or occupancy before the required certificate of occupancy.
